newsitem.title: USA: U.S., Japan shipping talks to continue Thursday.
newsitem.headline: U.S., Japan shipping talks to continue Thursday.

text.p: U.S. and Japanese maritime negotiators plan to continue talks aimed at averting U.S. sanctions against Japanese cargo vessels on Thursday, a Japanese official said.
The Japanese delegation, headed by Ministry of Transportation Director General Sadao Iwata, met Wednesday with State Department and Transportation Department officials, the Japanese official said.

The United States is set to slap $100,000 surcharges on Japanese vessels visiting U.S. ports in retaliation for what the Federal Maritime Commission said were unfair, restrictive practices at Japanese ports.

The FMC said the Japan Harbor Transportation Association (JHTA), which is made up of port cargo-handling firms and mediates between labor unions and shipping companies, has put in place costly and restrictive practices that discriminate against foreign vessels.
The surcharges are set to go into effect on April 14.
